subject: Renewal negotiation: analytics contract coverage & data-residency clarifications
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Kim <hannah.kim@amplitude.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal negotiation: analytics contract coverage & data-residency clarifications

Hi Hannah —

We just pulled the usage numbers for APIs + product events and the renewal window is coming up for our account (RDW-ANL-2026-07). Before we get an updated quote, two quick asks from Legal & Security: 

1) Data residency: we need to confirm that event storage and query processing for our EU region will remain in eu-west-1 for the next term. If the default is multi-region, can you list the options and any price delta?

2) Coverage: our API analytics consumption has grown ~25% QoQ — please confirm whether the tiered plan in your draft will cover projected spikes or if we should move to a committed throughput model.

Can you send an updated commercial quote and a version of the SOW (or DocuSign link) that includes the residency clause? I attached the usage export for May for reference.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if needed.

--
Rachel Kim
Senior Procurement Manager, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
[Attachment: analytics-usage-report-may2026.csv]
From: Hannah Kim <hannah.kim@amplitude.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@amplitude.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation: analytics contract coverage & data-residency clarifications

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the heads-up and the usage file. Quick answers below: 

- Data residency: we can lock storage + query processing to eu-west-1 for a hard residency guarantee. There is an optional add-on for region isolation (one-time configuration + +3% on the annual fee). If you prefer a soft residency (best-effort), there is no extra charge.

- Coverage: given the 25% growth, the committed throughput model will be more predictable for burst protection. I attached an updated quote (amplitude-quote-v2.pdf) that includes two options: (A) 12-month committed throughput + residency add-on, and (B) auto-scale with higher overage rates.

We can provision an SOW addendum that spells out residency. If that looks good I can route a DocuSign for signature. Would you like a walk-through of the pricing lines?

Regards,
Hannah
Account Executive — Amplitude
[Attachment: amplitude-quote-v2.pdf]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation: analytics contract coverage & data-residency clarifications

Thanks, Rachel / Hannah (copied from vendor).

Quick internal thoughts: 
- Legal: Laura, can you confirm if the +3% residency add-on is acceptable vs. our control requirements? If Legal needs a tighter SLA on access locality we should ask for the residency addendum to be put into the Master Services Agreement rather than an SOW, but that may slow timelines.

- Cost: Finance prefers committed throughput if it keeps overage exposure predictable; Marcus estimates committed will be ~10% cheaper than overage model at current forecast.

Action items: 
1) Laura to confirm legal position on placement of residency guarantee.
2) Rachel to ask Hannah for a version of the SOW with residency language and the DocuSign link.

--
Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Ops
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
[Attachment referenced: amplitude-quote-v2.pdf — forwarded in-thread]

Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation: analytics contract coverage & data-residency clarifications

Marking up the legal ask: we should request the residency language in an addendum to the MSA, not a standalone SOW. Rationale: SOWs are easier to replace/rotate across renewals and we want this to be a durable control. A 3% uplift is reasonable compared to the operational risk.

If Finance is aligned on committed throughput, approve negotiating option (A). Monica — can you confirm budget cadence so we can lock this before EOY procurement commit?

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation: analytics contract coverage & data-residency clarifications

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per internal alignment we are prepared to move forward on Option A (12-mo committed throughput) with the residency add-on, on the condition that the residency language is placed into an MSA addendum. Please route an SOW + MSA addendum reflecting that placement and send a DocuSign link for signature. 

Requested fields to confirm in the draft:
- Residency: eu-west-1 hard residency for storage + query processing
- SLA: maximum cross-region replication window 0 (no replication outside eu-west-1 without written consent)
- Pricing: committed throughput line and the +3% residency uplift (line-itemized)
- Term: 12 months with auto-renew unless 60-day termination notice

I'll loop Procurement once the DocuSign is live. If Legal needs a redline exchange we can turn around within 48 hours.

Best,
Rachel
Senior Procurement Manager, Redwood Inference
[Requested: DocuSign link + SOW addendum]
